summary: B1 revised Explore review completed with changes-requested. B1-RE-007 is resolved in substance: Q3 now provides a pure parser, Delivery-wide duplicate detection, monotonic validation, gap preservation, and explicit exhaustion behavior. One input-boundary gap remains in validateCandidateNnn: its number parameter has no stated finite-integer 001-999 validation, so zero, negative, fractional, or non-finite candidates are not explicitly rejected by the function that validates candidates.

blockingFindings.title: validateCandidateNnn does not validate its candidate as a valid NNN value
blockingFindings.evidence: The proposed validateCandidateNnn accepts a number and specifies rejection only for candidateNnn <= max(NNN) and candidateNnn > 999. It does not require a finite integer in the inclusive range 1 through 999, nor require tests for zero, negative, fractional, or non-finite input. The same Q3 defines NNN as the three-digit range 001-999.
blockingFindings.impact: The validator's public contract can accept a value that cannot be encoded as a valid NNN, especially when the existing set is empty or an implementation chooses no numeric lower bound for max. That defers rejection until a later formatter/parser rather than failing closed at the candidate-validation boundary.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Make validateCandidateNnn reject every candidate that is not a finite integer from 1 through 999 before evaluating monotonicity, using a machine-readable FlowkitError code. Add fixture tests for 0, a negative value, a fractional value, and non-finite input, as well as the existing monotonic/overflow/gap cases. Keep the returned/accepted candidate contract aligned with parseRunId's 001-999 grammar.

resolvedFindings.resolution: Q3 now defines pure format parsing, Delivery-wide NNN uniqueness, candidate monotonicity, allowed gaps, and NNN exhaustion without adding filesystem traversal to B1.
